provenance.instrument: Upper Gwynedd Township Code Chapter 195 Zoning (Ord. No. 87-11, 11-23-1987, as amended), as published on eCode360
provenance.status_detail: eCode360 code date 2025-12-08 (breadcrumb). New Laws on 2026-11-14 list two zoning amendments not yet in the code: Ord. No. 2026-01 and Ord. No. 2026-03 (both adopted 2026-05-11).
provenance.code_current_through_note: eCode360 breadcrumb 'Code 2025-12-08'. Chapter 195 adopted 11-23-1987 by Ord. No. 87-11.
provenance.code_caution: Two zoning amendments adopted 2026-05-11 (Ord. No. 2026-01 and 2026-03) are listed under New Laws and are not yet in the online code. Their text was not read. Code search excerpts show Ord. No. 2026-01 rewrites the definitions of dwelling unit and family (adding unrelated individuals who maintain a common household) and wording on short-term rentals. Ask the township whether either changes the rule on a separate living area for relatives.
checks: The code has no accessory dwelling unit term. Its rule is an accessory use: 'When accessory to a single-family detached dwelling only, one separate living area, including cooking facilities, may be provided for no more than two persons related to the principal occupant' by blood, marriage or adoption (195-9F(1)(g))

No change may be made in the area covered by the building that houses it: no enlargement of the building's footprint (195-9F(1)(g)). The code reads 'building' as if followed by 'or part thereof' and counts a shed, garage or carport as a building (195-3A, B), so an existing accessory building is not excluded. A building accessory to a dwelling is at most 14 ft tall (195-9M(2))
It is registered with the Zoning Officer, with a recorded written agreement to remove the cooking facilities when the relatives no longer use them (195-9F(1)(g))

R-1 lists accessory uses 'subject to the provisions of § 195-9F' (195-11A(4)), VPR and VC list accessory uses customarily incidental to the permitted uses (195-17B(5), 195-18B(14)). R-3 and R-4 list only a private garage, private parking space or outbuildings as permitted accessory uses (195-13B(8), 195-14B(5)). R-2, AP ('for the following purposes and no other') and BP list no accessory use (195-12A, 195-26.2B, 195-10B). Whether the separate living area reaches R-2, R-3, R-4, AP and BP is not settled. The Zoning Hearing Board decides whether a use is customarily incidental to a permitted use (195-53A)

A dwelling unit is 'A building or portion thereof providing complete housekeeping facilities for one family' (195-3B). R-3 and VPR bar any dwelling unit with less than 800 sq ft of living space and any living quarters below grade (195-13G(2), (3), 195-17C(2)). The code does not call the separate living area a dwelling unit. Ask whether these rules reach it

In VPR, converting a single-family dwelling into a residence for more families is a special exception. The property is treated as if zoned R-2 and must meet all R-2 rules (21,780 sq ft lot). The Board sets the number of families. Two parking spaces per unit (195-17B(6)(c), 195-28A(10))
Two-family dwellings (twins and duplexes) are permitted by right in VPR and VC: 7,000 sq ft of lot and 40 ft of width per dwelling unit, public sewer and water (195-17B(2), C(1)(b), 195-18B(11))
R-3 permits duplexes and twin duplexes only within a development tract of at least five acres, at most 15% of the units (195-13B(5), (6), D)

C permits no single-family detached dwelling ('any one of the following purposes and no other'). A combined commercial and single-family residential use in one structure is a special exception on 21,780 sq ft (195-22A(8)(h), C). GA permits only apartment houses (195-16B). IN permits single-family detached dwellings only for people 55 and over, as a conditional use (195-26B(12), F(3))
BP and VC permit one dwelling unit in a mixed-use structure with offices or shops (195-10B(1)(c), 195-18B(12), (13)). It is not a second unit for a house

Accessory structures may not stand in the required front yard, nor (except a detached garage) between the house and a street line (195-9G(1)). A building accessory to a dwelling may be at most 14 ft tall (195-9M(2))
provenance.notes: Zoning office: Upper Gwynedd Township Code Enforcement and Building and Zoning Department. eCode360 code UP0929 is Upper Gwynedd Township, Montgomery County (leases recorded with the Recorder of Deeds of Montgomery County, 195-9S(2)(h)). Read on eCode360 in a browser, one page at a time, on 2026-11-14. Code search (all content, New Laws included) for accessory apartment, accessory dwelling, in-law, ECHO, elder cottage, granny, family dwelling, relative, housekeeping unit, caretaker, guest house, accessory living, tenant house, living quarters, sleeping quarters, immediate family and watchman found no ADU term. A second search for conversion, two-family, duplex, second dwelling and apartment found 195-17 (VPR), 195-13, 195-16 and 195-28. The separate living area rule (195-9F(1)(g)) was found by reading 195-9 in full. The site search did not return it for 'separate living' or 'cooking facilities', and did not return VC 195-18B(11) for 'two-family', so every district section was opened directly. Read in full: 195-3 (word usage and all definitions), 195-9, 195-10 (BP), 195-11, 195-12, 195-13, 195-14, 195-16 (GA), 195-17, 195-18, 195-19, 195-21, 195-22 (C), 195-26 (IN), 195-26.2, 195-27, 195-53. Read in part: 195-10.1 (B), 195-21.1 (TOD-2), 195-28, the Chapter 195 contents. Not read: TH 195-14.1, MH 195-15, OC 195-20, SC 195-23, LI 195-25, I 195-26.1, Article VIII (nonconformities), 195-55, the two New Laws (PDF). Fix round 2026-11-14 after an independent review: C, GA and IN moved out of the reach of the rule, AP and BP added to the district-reach condition, BP row added, the footprint rule reworded, the VC accessory yard note corrected.

term.value: separate living area, including cooking facilities, for relatives (accessory use)
term.note: 'When accessory to a single-family detached dwelling only, one separate living area, including cooking facilities, may be provided for no more than two persons related to the principal occupant of the single-family detached dwelling by blood, marriage or adoption'. The code has no ADU term.

status.note: An accessory use for up to two relatives of the principal occupant, in an existing building with no enlargement of its footprint. No hearing: it is registered with the Zoning Officer.

scope_by_use.note: The rule is accessory to a single-family detached dwelling, which R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4, VPR, VC, AP and BP permit. R-2, AP and BP list no accessory use and R-3 and R-4 list only garages, parking and outbuildings, so the reach there is a reading. B lists no dwelling. C permits uses 'for any one of the following purposes and no other', with no single-family detached dwelling. Only a combined commercial and single-family residential use in one structure, by special exception (195-22A(8)(h)). GA permits only apartment houses (195-16B). IN permits single-family detached dwellings only for people 55 and over, by conditional use (195-26B(12)). TH, MH, OC, SC, LI and I were not read.

status_outside.note: The rule needs a single-family detached dwelling.

path.note: An accessory use the chapter authorizes. A zoning permit (195-48A) and registration with the Zoning Officer, with a recorded agreement to remove the cooking facilities later.

fallback_path.note: The Zoning Hearing Board may authorize a variance 'where, owing to special conditions, a literal enforcement of the provisions of this chapter will result in unnecessary hardship'. No special exception for uses not listed was found. The Board also interprets whether a use is customarily incidental to a permitted use (195-53A).

value.name: Conversion of a single-family dwelling for more families (VPR)
value.conditions: Zoning Hearing Board special exception for 'The conversion of a single-family dwelling into a residence for a greater number of families'. The property is treated as though zoned R-2 and must meet all R-2 rules (lot 21,780 sq ft and 120 ft wide, yards 50, 25 and 50 ft, buildings at most 20% of the lot). Outside stairways enclosed, two means of exit per unit. The Board sets the number of families and may add conditions. Public sewer and water. Two parking spaces per dwelling unit.
value.note: Not an ADU listing. No family rule. The R-2 lot of 21,780 sq ft is read as the lot the converted building needs

value.name: Two-family dwelling (twin or duplex) in VPR or VC
value.conditions: Two-family dwellings (twins and duplexes) are permitted. Per dwelling unit 7,000 sq ft of lot and 40 ft of width, so 14,000 sq ft and 80 ft for two units. Front yard 30 ft. Duplex side yards 10 ft, 30 ft together. Rear yard 40 ft. Buildings at most 25% and impervious cover 40% of the lot. Public sewer and water. Two parking spaces per dwelling unit. VC uses the VPR standards (195-18B(11)).
value.note: Not an ADU listing. Whether adding a unit to an existing house is read as this use is not said. A duplex is 'A building having two separate dwelling units, one over the other' (195-3B)

value.name: Duplex or twin duplex in an R-3 development
value.conditions: Two-family detached (over-and-under duplex) and twin duplex dwellings are permitted, only within a development tract of at least five acres with two or more housing types, at most 15% of the units in duplexes and five units per developable acre. A duplex lot is at least 10,800 sq ft and 72 ft wide, rear yard 48 ft, side yards 12 ft (30 ft together), front 30 ft, impervious cover 15%. Two parking spaces per unit.
value.note: Not an ADU listing. A development use on a tract of five acres, not a unit added to one house

value.name: One dwelling unit in a mixed-use structure (BP, VC)
value.conditions: A mixed-use structure with permitted offices or shops and at most one dwelling unit. BP: lot 20,000 sq ft and the BP dimensional table, public sewer and water. VC: commercial lot 8,000 sq ft, 40 ft wide, building coverage 25%, impervious cover 80%. A dwelling unit needs two parking spaces on the lot.
value.note: Not an ADU listing. A building that pairs a business use with one dwelling unit, not a second unit for a house

value.name: Combined commercial and single-family residential use in one structure (C)
value.conditions: Zoning Hearing Board special exception for a combined commercial and single-family residential use in one structure, the commercial use of a type permitted in C. Lot 21,780 sq ft and 120 ft wide, buildings at most 20% of the lot, front yard 60 ft on each street, side yards 25 ft (60 ft together), rear yard 50 ft.
value.note: Not an ADU listing. C permits no single-family detached dwelling, only this combined use

zoning_districts.note: Wherever a single-family detached dwelling is permitted. R-1 names 195-9F expressly (195-11A(4)). In IN only an age-restricted house approved as a conditional use.

building_types.note: 'When accessory to a single-family detached dwelling only'. A single-family detached dwelling has 'no party or common wall' and is 'completely surrounded by its own yard'.

existing_structure_only.note: 'Provided that no change is made in the area covered by the building in which housed'. No enlargement of the building's footprint. The building may be the house or an existing accessory building (195-3A, B).

value.condition: For no more than two persons related to the principal occupant of the single-family detached dwelling by blood, marriage or adoption.

No enlargement of the building's footprint: no change may be made in the area covered by the building in which the living area is housed. An existing accessory building such as a garage or shed is a building under the code and is not excluded.
Registered with the Zoning Officer, with a recorded written agreement to remove the cooking facilities when the relatives no longer use them.

R-3 and R-4 list only a private garage, private parking space or outbuildings as permitted accessory uses. R-2, AP and BP list no accessory use (AP 'for the following purposes and no other', BP 'any one of the following uses'). Whether the separate living area reaches these districts is not settled. Ask the zoning officer.
Lots in R-1, R-3, VPR, VC and BP are to be served by public sewer and public water.

Lots in a PSR planned single-family subdivision (in R-1 or R-2), a lot averaging subdivision (R-1, R-2, AP), an R-3 optional reduced lot size development or an R-3 redevelopment subdivision take that plan's smaller lots and yards: PSR R-1 35,000 sq ft with side yards of 30 ft, PSR R-2 17,400 sq ft with side yards of 20 ft. Lot averaging: lots up to 20% smaller, R-1 front 45 ft and sides 20 ft (50 ft together), R-2 front 35 ft and sides 15 ft (40 ft together). R-3 reduced lot size 7,000 sq ft with a front yard of 25 ft and side yards of 10 ft. R-3 redevelopment subdivision (conditional use on a 1.5 to 5 acre tract of pre-1942 lots): 6,000 sq ft, front 25 ft, sides 10 ft, rear 35 ft, impervious cover 40%, 35 ft high.

R-3 and VPR bar a dwelling unit with less than 800 sq ft of living space (basements excluded) and living quarters below grade. The code does not call the separate living area a dwelling unit. Ask whether this reaches it.

In IN a single-family detached dwelling is only for age-restricted housing: every unit has at least one permanent resident 55 or older, and children of the occupant must be 18 or older except for holiday and summer stays.

districts_read_no_listing.note: B lists no dwelling. TOD and TOD-2 are overlays for tract developments of apartments, multiple-family and townhouse dwellings by conditional use (20 acres and four acres).

types_allowed.note: Inside the existing house, with no enlargement of its footprint.

types_not_addressed.note: The rule speaks of 'the building in which housed' and does not say it must be the house. 'Building' includes a shed, garage, carport or other accessory building and is read 'or part thereof' (195-3A, B), so an existing garage or outbuilding is not excluded, but it is not named either. The footprint may not grow. A unit over a garage is in practice capped by the 14 ft height for a building accessory to a dwelling (195-9M(2)).

value.internal: Separate living area for relatives inside the house

max_sqft.note: No size cap is written. The living area may not enlarge the area the building covers.

accessory_structure_max_height_ft.note: 'For any building accessory to any dwelling use: 14 feet.' R-4 repeats it (195-14D(4)).

front_yard_barred.note: 'Structures accessory to a permitted use shall not be permitted within the required front yard of a lot and, with the exception of a detached garage ... shall not be permitted on that portion of the lot between the principal building and the lot line that abuts a street right-of-way.'

owner_occupancy.note: No owner rule. The relatives must be related to the principal occupant.

occupancy.value: At most two persons related to the principal occupant of the house by blood, marriage or adoption.

spaces_required.note: No parking rule for the separate living area.

reading.value: No parking rule for the separate living area. A dwelling unit needs two spaces on the same lot (195-28A(1)). If the living area were counted as a second dwelling unit the lot would need four. A dwelling converted to apartments needs two spaces for each unit (195-28A(10)).

min_lot_sqft.note: Lot width 200 ft. Public sewer and water (195-11C).

max_building_coverage.note: 'Not more than 10% of the area of each lot may be occupied by buildings.'

accessory_setback_side_ft.note: An accessory building constructed separately may stand in the side and rear yards, not in a yard abutting a street, at least this far from the line and behind the front wall line of the house.

min_lot_sqft.note: Lot width 120 ft. Existing undersized lots may place patios, decks and one-story attached garage additions 20 ft from a side line and 40 ft from the rear line (195-12C).

max_building_coverage.note: 'Not more than 20% of the area of each lot may be occupied by buildings.'

accessory_setback_side_ft.note: An accessory building constructed separately may stand in the side and rear yards, not in a yard abutting a street, at least this far from the line and behind the front wall line of the house.

min_lot_sqft.note: Single-family detached: 8,400 sq ft, 60 ft wide. The optional reduced lot size is 7,000 sq ft with a front yard of 25 ft and side yards of 10 ft (195-13F). Uses need a five-acre development tract (195-13D).

principal_max_height_ft.note: 'No building shall be constructed to a height greater than 28 feet.'

max_impervious_coverage.note: Maximum impervious cover 35% for a single-family detached dwelling. No building coverage figure.

accessory_setback_side_ft.note: An accessory building constructed separately may stand in the side and rear yards, not in a yard abutting a street, at least this far from the line and behind the front wall line of the house.

min_lot_sqft.note: Single-family detached: 11,000 sq ft, 80 ft wide. Uses need a five-acre tract (195-14D(1)).

principal_max_height_ft.note: 'No building shall be constructed to a height greater than 28 feet.' Accessory buildings 14 ft (195-14D(4)).

max_impervious_coverage.note: Maximum impervious cover 20%. No building coverage figure.

accessory_setback_side_ft.note: An accessory building constructed separately may stand in the side and rear yards, not in a yard abutting a street, at least this far from the line and behind the front wall line of the house.

min_lot_sqft.note: Single-family detached house: 9,800 sq ft, 80 ft wide. Two-family dwelling: 7,000 sq ft and 40 ft per dwelling unit (195-17C(1)(b)). Public sewer and water (195-17C(3)).

max_building_coverage.note: 'Maximum building coverage: 25%.' Lot coverage 40% (all impervious material).

accessory_setback_side_ft.note: An accessory building constructed separately may stand in the side and rear yards, not in a yard abutting a street, at least this far from the line and behind the front wall line of the house.

min_lot_sqft.note: A single-family or two-family dwelling follows the VPR standards (195-18B(11)). Commercial uses need 8,000 sq ft (195-18C(1)). Accessory buildings stand in the rear yard only, 6 ft from the rear line and 2 ft from a side line (195-18C(5)).

max_building_coverage.note: VPR standards for a dwelling. Commercial uses: building coverage 25%, impervious 80%.

max_impervious_coverage.note: VPR standard for a dwelling: lot coverage 40% (all impervious material). Commercial uses 80%.

accessory_setback_side_ft.note: An accessory building constructed separately may be erected within the rear yard only, no nearer than 6 ft to the rear lot line and 2 ft to a side lot line.

min_lot_sqft.note: Lots for single-family detached dwellings 43,560 sq ft, with the R-1 rules.

max_building_coverage.note: Single-family lots follow the R-1 area and width rules (195-26.2C(3)).

accessory_setback_side_ft.note: An accessory building constructed separately may stand in the side and rear yards, not in a yard abutting a street, at least this far from the line and behind the front wall line of the house.

min_lot_sqft.note: Single-family detached dwelling under 195-10B(1)(d): 20,000 sq ft, 100 ft wide at the building line. Any yard abutting a street meets the 60 ft front yard. Yards abutting a residential district 75 ft. Public sewer and water (195-10H(1)).

principal_max_height_ft.note: 'No building or structure ... shall exceed 35 feet.'

max_building_coverage.note: '15% to 30%' by formula: 15% plus 15% times (lot area minus 20,000 sq ft) divided by 20,000. 15% on a 20,000 sq ft lot, 30% at 40,000 sq ft. The lowest figure is stored.

adu_path.note: IN permits single-family detached dwellings only for occupancy by people 55 and over, approved as a conditional use by the Board of Commissioners (195-26B(12)). Accessory uses customarily incidental to the permitted uses are allowed (195-26B(14)). The living area would be accessory to such a house. Whether it needs its own approval is not settled. Ask the township.
